constraints:
• 1 <= n <= 10^5
  • 0 <= edges.length <= 2 * 10^5
  • edges[i] = [u, v] with 0 <= u, v < n
  • The graph is undirected; repeated edges and cycles may appear.
why: The first graph skill: count connected components. Start a DFS or BFS from every node not yet visited; each start is a new component, and the traversal marks the whole component so it is never counted twice.
hints: Pick any node and visit everything reachable from it. What have you just found?
Every node belongs to exactly one component. Loop over the nodes; when you meet an unvisited one, increase the count and flood its whole component with DFS or BFS.
Build an adjacency list (add both directions), keep a visited array, and use an explicit stack so deep graphs do not hit Python's recursion limit. O(n + edges).
pitfalls: Isolated nodes with no edges are components too; loop over all n nodes, not over the edges.
Mark a node visited when you push it, not when you pop it, or it can be pushed many times.
